texts.title: The return of the night train

paragraphs.text: For most of the twentieth century the sleeper was an ordinary way to cross Europe. You boarded in one capital in the evening, ate in the dining car, and woke up in another. Then, in the 1990s, cheap flights arrived, and the night train began to look like a museum piece. One operator after another withdrew its sleeping cars: between 2000 and 2015 dozens of routes were cut, and several national railways left the business altogether. The rolling stock was sold, scrapped or left to rust in sidings. What happened next surprised almost everyone. From about 2016 the direction of travel reversed. An Austrian operator bought sleeping cars that a larger neighbour no longer wanted, put them back on the rails, and began adding routes rather than closing them.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: To understand why the sleeper nearly died, it helps to look at the arithmetic rather than the romance. A carriage full of seats can hold eighty passengers; the same carriage fitted with berths holds perhaps thirty, and a carriage of single compartments holds fewer still. Staff must be on board through the night, which no daytime service requires. The train needs a path across the network at the very hours when engineers want the track to themselves, because maintenance of the track is usually carried out at night. And the vehicles themselves are specialised: a sleeping car cannot be used for anything else, so it earns money only when the route runs.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The return of the sleeper has less to do with nostalgia than with carbon. A short flight releases far more greenhouse gas per passenger than the equivalent rail journey, and by the end of the 2010s enough travellers had noticed for the shift to show up in ticket sales. In Sweden a word for the unease of flying entered ordinary speech. Large companies began to write rail into their travel policies, partly to cut reported emissions and partly because staff asked for it. Governments moved too: one European country has banned domestic flights on routes where the train takes under two and a half hours. None of these measures was aimed at night trains in particular, but together they changed the question a traveller asks from “how fast?” to “at what cost?”.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Operators who studied their own passengers found that comfort mattered less than they had assumed. What people wanted was sleep and privacy, in that order, and to be delivered somewhere useful. A night train sets its passengers down in the city centre at breakfast time, with no airport transfer at either end, and passengers value arriving in the city centre far more than they value a wider bed. The newest vehicles answer this directly. Alongside the traditional six-berth couchette there are now single compartments for travellers who do not want to share with strangers, sealed pods with a door and a locker, and quieter bogies, because a passenger who is woken four times has not really travelled overnight at all.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: The obstacles that remain are mostly administrative. A night train crosses three or four borders while its passengers sleep, and the operator needs approval from the regulator in every country it passes through, under rules that were written for freight and commuter traffic. Electrical systems and signalling still differ from one network to the next, so a locomotive that works in one country may be useless in the next. Then there is the queue for vehicles: the factories that build sleeping cars are few, and an order placed today is delivered in years, not months. Night services must also compete with freight trains for space on the network at night, and freight has the older claim.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: It would be easy to oversell all this. The sleeper is not going to replace aviation, and the routes that work are a particular shape: long enough that the journey fills a night, short enough that it does not fill two. Between roughly 800 and 1,500 kilometres the night train is competitive; beyond that the plane wins on time and below it the day train wins on convenience. The honest measure of the revival is therefore not how many routes are announced, which is easy, but whether a route survives a decade, which is not. On that measure the evidence is encouraging but thin, and the next ten years will settle the argument better than any forecast can.
paragraphs.label: F

texts.title: How honey bees choose a home

paragraphs.text: In late spring a honey bee colony that has outgrown its home divides. About half the workers leave with the old queen and settle on a branch nearby in a cluster the size of a football. The cluster is a temporary thing: it has no comb, no store of honey and no shelter, and if it is still hanging there in a week the bees will die. From this cluster a few hundred of the oldest workers fly out as scouts, and within a day or two the swarm will move, in one flight, to a cavity that none of the other bees has seen. The colony is therefore about to take the most consequential decision of its life, with no leader, no plan and no way of comparing the options side by side.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: What a scout is looking for turns out to be surprisingly precise. She measures the inside of a hollow tree by walking over its surfaces and by making short flights across it in the dark, and she is measuring against a specification. The cavity should hold about forty litres: much smaller and the colony cannot store enough honey for winter, much larger and it cannot keep the space warm. The entrance should be small, a few square centimetres, so that it can be defended, and it should be several metres above the ground, away from most animals that raid nests. The cavity must be dry and it must be sound. A scout that finds all of this in one place has found something rare.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A scout that is satisfied returns to the cluster and dances on its surface. The dance is the same one bees use for flowers: a figure of eight whose straight run points towards the site and whose length encodes the distance. What matters for the decision is how long the dancer keeps dancing. A site that only just meets the specification earns a handful of circuits; an excellent one earns dozens, repeated over many minutes. The scout is not describing the site in detail. She is advertising it with an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be, and other idle scouts in the cluster read that effort and fly off to look for themselves.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: This is where a crowd of opinions becomes a single choice. A scout that returns from a second visit dances a little less than she did the first time, and less again after the third, so every advertisement fades unless it is renewed. Sites that impress few visitors lose their dancers within hours. Sites that impress many gain them faster than they lose them, and the cluster gradually falls silent about everything except one hollow tree. Crucially, the bees do not wait for agreement. The choice is settled by a quorum: once about fifteen scouts are found at one site at the same time, that site has won, even though most of the swarm has never been there and some scouts are still dancing for somewhere else.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Reaching the quorum changes what the scouts do. They fly back and move through the cluster producing a thin, rising sound that researchers call piping, pressing themselves against their motionless sisters as they go. The piping is not an instruction about direction; it is an instruction about time. A bee cannot fly until the muscles in her thorax are close to thirty-five degrees, and warming them takes several minutes. Piping tells the cluster to warm its flight muscles, and about ten minutes later ten thousand bees lift off together. Only then do the scouts, now flying as guides through the cloud of their sisters, steer the swarm towards the site they chose.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Does the system actually work? The test is blunt: a colony that chooses badly does not survive the winter, and the cost of a poor cavity is paid months after the decision is made. Researchers have measured this by offering swarms a choice of wooden boxes of known size and following the colonies afterwards. Swarms nearly always take the box that matches the specification, even when a poorer box is closer, and colonies in the right-sized boxes are far more likely to be alive in spring. When a swarm is given only poor options it takes one anyway, because hanging on a branch is not an option at all, and those colonies do badly.
paragraphs.label: F

paragraphs.text: The reason this small piece of natural history is quoted so often outside biology is the shape of the procedure rather than the bees. The scouts assess the options independently, each seeing a site for herself before saying anything about it. They advertise in proportion to what they found, so a weak case fades on its own instead of having to be defeated. And the group stops when enough of its members have converged, not when the last doubter has been persuaded. Committees that copy the first two habits and ignore the third tend to talk until someone gives way; the bees are on the wing by then, which is perhaps the most useful thing about them.
paragraphs.label: G

paragraphs.text: Ask who speaks English and the honest answer is: mostly people who learned it later. By any reasonable count, speakers who acquired English as a second or foreign language outnumber those who grew up with it by something like three to one, and most conversations held in English today take place with no first-language speaker present at all. A meeting between a Korean engineer and a Brazilian buyer is not an unusual case of English use; it is the ordinary case. This simple arithmetic has an awkward consequence for language teaching, which has spent a century treating the speech of a minority as the target that everyone else should aim at. It also raises a question that sounds philosophical and is in fact entirely practical: if English now belongs mostly to the people who learned it, whose version of it should a classroom teach?
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Ana Duarte has spent twenty years arguing that the target is wrong. The purpose of learning English, she says, is to be understood by whoever is in the room, and the room is rarely in London. From recordings of international meetings she has drawn up what she calls a core: the features of pronunciation that actually carry meaning between speakers of different first languages. Get those right, she argues, and your accent is your own business. A national model should not be the target of teaching, because it asks learners to spend years on features that no listener in their working life will need, and it quietly tells them that their own voice is a defect to be corrected.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Martin Keel is not persuaded, and his objection is practical rather than sentimental. Ask learners what they want, he says, and a large majority name a national model, usually British or American; teachers who offer them something else are overruling the people who paid for the course. Worse, the institutions that decide learners’ futures have not moved. Examiners, universities and employers still listen with an ear trained on those models, and a candidate who has been taught an international variety is judged by a standard nobody taught her. Until the gatekeepers change, he argues, teaching to an international core leaves learners short of what they are actually measured against.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Ruth Oyelaran suspects that both of them are arguing about the wrong thing. The dispute looks like a question about pronunciation, she writes, but it is really a question about authority: who writes the textbooks, who sets the tests, whose usage gets printed as an error in the margin. English in Nigeria and India is not a stage on the way to something else. These are varieties with their own settled norms, their own literatures and their own generations of speakers who learned them at home, and describing them as approximations tells you nothing about the language and a good deal about who is doing the describing. The point is not that every variety is equally useful in every room, but that the map of correctness is drawn by somebody, and the somebody is rarely the speakers being corrected.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Tomas Vrba brings evidence rather than argument. In his experiments, listeners from a dozen language backgrounds hear recordings that have been altered one feature at a time, and he measures what they actually fail to understand. The results are uneven in a useful way. Consonants at the beginning of words, and the difference between long and short vowels, cause real breakdowns when they go wrong; vowel quality, the feature that most accent training concentrates on, causes remarkably few. Word stress in long words matters more than either. A teacher with limited hours, he concludes, can now choose what to fix on evidence instead of on habit. None of this settles the argument about ownership, but it does narrow the part of the argument that a timetable has to answer.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Where does this leave a classroom on Monday morning? Not, honestly, in a settled place. The examinations that decide admissions are slow to change and still reward a familiar sound, so Keel’s objection has force whatever one thinks of the principle. But the published descriptions of what has to be taught have narrowed, and the evidence about what actually interrupts understanding is better than it was. Perhaps the most useful thing a teacher can do is stop treating the question as general. A learner who wants to work in a hospital in Manchester and a learner who will spend her career in meetings between Jakarta and Frankfurt do not need the same pronunciation course, and pretending otherwise serves neither of them. The question worth asking in a staffroom is therefore not whose English is correct, but what this particular learner has to be able to do with it.
paragraphs.label: F

topic.en: Three texts: the return of night trains, how a swarm of bees picks a new home, and the argument over whose English counts as correct.
topic.kk: Үш мәтін: түнгі пойыздардың қайта оралуы, ара үйірі жаңа баспананы қалай таңдайды және кімнің ағылшыны дұрыс деген талқы.
topic.ru: Три текста: возвращение ночных поездов, как пчелиный рой выбирает новое жильё и спор о том, чей английский считать правильным.

items.quote: between 2000 and 2015 dozens of routes were cut, and several national railways left the business altogether
items.prompt: Several national railways stopped running sleeper services before 2016.

explanation.en: “several national railways left the business altogether” before 2016 → TRUE. “Left the business” is simply another way of saying they stopped running the service.
explanation.kk: «several national railways left the business altogether» — 2016 жылға дейін → TRUE. «Left the business» тіркесі «тоқтатты» дегенді басқаша айтып тұр.
explanation.ru: «several national railways left the business altogether» до 2016 года → TRUE. «Left the business» и есть «перестали возить», просто другими словами.

items.quote: A carriage full of seats can hold eighty passengers; the same carriage fitted with berths holds perhaps thirty
items.prompt: A carriage with berths takes fewer passengers than the same carriage with seats.

explanation.en: Eighty seats against roughly thirty berths → TRUE. The numbers are not a trap here but a direct comparison of the same carriage.
explanation.kk: 80 орын мен шамамен 30 жатын орын салыстырылады → TRUE. Мұндағы сандар тұзақ емес, бір вагонның тікелей салыстыруы.
explanation.ru: 80 мест против примерно 30 спальных → TRUE. Числа здесь не ловушка, а прямое сравнение одного и того же вагона.

items.quote: a sleeping car cannot be used for anything else, so it earns money only when the route runs
items.prompt: Night services earn more profit than daytime services on the same route.
keywords: earns money only when the route runs

explanation.en: Paragraph B lists the costs of a night train, but the profit of day and night services is never compared → NOT GIVEN. FALSE would need a sentence saying daytime services earn more.
explanation.kk: B абзацы түнгі пойыздың шығынын тізеді, бірақ күндізгі мен түнгі рейстің табысы еш жерде салыстырылмайды → NOT GIVEN. FALSE деу үшін күндізгісі көбірек табады деген сөйлем керек еді.
explanation.ru: Абзац B перечисляет расходы ночного поезда, но прибыль дневного и ночного рейса нигде не сравнивается → NOT GIVEN. Для FALSE нужна была бы фраза о том, что дневной зарабатывает больше.

items.quote: A short flight releases far more greenhouse gas per passenger than the equivalent rail journey
items.prompt: Flying produces more greenhouse gas per passenger than travelling the same distance by train.
keywords: far more greenhouse gas per passenger

explanation.en: “far more greenhouse gas per passenger than the equivalent rail journey” → TRUE. “Equivalent rail journey” is exactly “the same distance by train”.
explanation.kk: «far more greenhouse gas per passenger than the equivalent rail journey» → TRUE. «Equivalent rail journey» дегеніміз — сол қашықтықты пойызбен жүру.
explanation.ru: «far more greenhouse gas per passenger than the equivalent rail journey» → TRUE. «Equivalent rail journey» — это и есть «то же расстояние поездом».

items.quote: one European country has banned domestic flights on routes where the train takes under two and a half hours
items.prompt: The ban on short flights applies in every European country.

explanation.en: The text says “one European country” and only domestic flights → FALSE. The statement widens one country to the whole of Europe — a classic over-generalisation trap.
explanation.kk: Мәтінде «one European country» және тек ішкі рейстер → FALSE. Тұжырым бір елді бүкіл Еуропаға дейін кеңейтіп тұр — жалпылау тұзағы.
explanation.ru: В тексте «one European country» и только внутренние рейсы → FALSE. Утверждение расширяет одну страну до всей Европы — классическая ловушка на обобщение.

items.quote: an order placed today is delivered in years, not months
items.prompt: New sleeping cars can be delivered a few months after they are ordered.

explanation.en: “delivered in years, not months” directly contradicts the statement → FALSE. The text itself rules out “months”, so this is not NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: «delivered in years, not months» тұжырымға тікелей қайшы → FALSE. Мәтін «айлар» нұсқасын өзі теріске шығарады, сондықтан бұл NOT GIVEN емес.
explanation.ru: «delivered in years, not months» прямо противоречит утверждению → FALSE. Текст сам снимает вариант «месяцы», поэтому это не NOT GIVEN.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Text 1? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

items.quote: there are now single compartments for travellers who do not want to share with strangers
items.prompt: Travellers who prefer not to share with strangers can now book 7 ____.

explanation.en: “single compartments for travellers who do not want to share” → single compartments. The “traditional six-berth couchette” nearby is the shared option, not the answer.
explanation.kk: «single compartments for travellers who do not want to share» → single compartments. Қасындағы «traditional six-berth couchette» ортақ вагон туралы, жауап емес.
explanation.ru: «single compartments for travellers who do not want to share» → single compartments. «Traditional six-berth couchette» рядом — про общий вагон, это не ответ.

items.quote: Night services must also compete with freight trains for space on the network at night
items.prompt: At night, sleeper services have to compete for track space with 8 ____.

explanation.en: “compete with freight trains for space on the network at night” → freight trains. The word “compete” appears in both the question and the text, so it is quick to locate.
explanation.kk: «compete with freight trains for space on the network at night» → freight trains. Сұрақтағы «compete» сөзі мәтінде де сол күйінде тұр, сондықтан тез табылады.
explanation.ru: «compete with freight trains for space on the network at night» → freight trains. Слово «compete» в вопросе и в тексте одно и то же, поэтому находится быстро.

items.quote: maintenance of the track is usually carried out at night
items.prompt: Work on the track itself normally takes place 9 ____.

explanation.en: “maintenance of the track is usually carried out at night” → at night. “Work on the track” in the question is “maintenance” in the text.
explanation.kk: «maintenance of the track is usually carried out at night» → at night. Сұрақтағы «work on the track» — мәтіндегі «maintenance».
explanation.ru: «maintenance of the track is usually carried out at night» → at night. «Work on the track» в вопросе — это «maintenance» в тексте.

items.quote: Between roughly 800 and 1,500 kilometres the night train is competitive
items.prompt: Night trains compete best on journeys of between 800 and 10 ____ kilometres.

explanation.en: “Between roughly 800 and 1,500 kilometres” → 1,500. The paragraph also contains “a decade” and “800” — the answer is the upper end of the range, not the lower.
explanation.kk: «Between roughly 800 and 1,500 kilometres» → 1,500. Абзацта «a decade» де, «800» де бар — аралықтың бірінші емес, екінші шекарасы керек.
explanation.ru: «Between roughly 800 and 1,500 kilometres» → 1,500. В абзаце есть и «a decade», и «800» — берём вторую границу диапазона, а не первую.

groups.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER from Text 1 for each answer.

items.quote: A night train sets its passengers down in the city centre at breakfast time
items.prompt: Where does a night train deliver its passengers in the morning?

explanation.en: “sets its passengers down in the city centre at breakfast time” → the city centre. The American spelling center is also accepted.
explanation.kk: «sets its passengers down in the city centre at breakfast time» → the city centre. Американдық center емлесі де есептеледі.
explanation.ru: «sets its passengers down in the city centre at breakfast time» → the city centre. Американское написание center тоже засчитывается.

items.quote: the operator needs approval from the regulator in every country it passes through
items.prompt: What does an operator need from the regulator in each country on the route?

explanation.en: “needs approval from the regulator in every country” → approval. There is no need to write the whole phrase “approval from the regulator”: the limit is three words and the question asks what is needed.
explanation.kk: «needs approval from the regulator in every country» → approval. «approval from the regulator» тіркесін толық жазудың қажеті жоқ: шек — үш сөз, сұрақ «нені» дегенді сұрайды.
explanation.ru: «needs approval from the regulator in every country» → approval. Целую фразу «approval from the regulator» писать не нужно: лимит — три слова, и вопрос спрашивает именно «что».

items.quote: whether a route survives a decade, which is not
items.prompt: According to the writer, how long must a route last before the revival can be judged?

explanation.en: “the honest measure … is … whether a route survives a decade” → a decade. “Ten years” is also accepted. “The next ten years” in the final sentence refers to the argument, not to how long a route lasts.
explanation.kk: «the honest measure … is … whether a route survives a decade» → a decade. «Ten years» нұсқасы да қабылданады. Соңғы сөйлемдегі «the next ten years» бағыттың емес, талқының мерзімі.
explanation.ru: «the honest measure … is … whether a route survives a decade» → a decade. «Ten years» тоже принимается. «The next ten years» в последнем предложении — про спор в целом, а не про срок жизни маршрута.

groups.instruction: Answer the questions below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from Text 1 for each answer.

items.quote: The cavity should hold about forty litres
items.prompt: Paragraph B

explanation.en: Paragraph B is a list of measurements: volume, entrance, height, dryness → iii. Heading ix is about winter warmth: warmth is mentioned as the reason for the size, not as the topic of the paragraph.
explanation.kk: B абзацы — өлшемдер тізімі: көлем, кіреберіс, биіктік, құрғақтық → iii. ix тақырыбы қысқы жылу туралы: жылу көлемнің себебі ретінде аталған, абзацтың тақырыбы емес.
explanation.ru: Абзац B — это перечень мерок: объём, вход, высота, сухость → iii. Заголовок ix про зимнее тепло: тепло упомянуто как причина размера, а не как тема абзаца.

items.quote: She is advertising it with an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be
items.prompt: Paragraph C

explanation.en: The whole of paragraph C is about the dance as advertising: its length shows the scout’s judgement → v. The word “advertising” appears in the text itself.
explanation.kk: C абзацының бәрі биді жарнама ретінде сипаттайды: бидің ұзақтығы бағаны көрсетеді → v. «Advertising» сөзі мәтінде тікелей тұр.
explanation.ru: Весь абзац C — про танец как рекламу: длина танца показывает оценку → v. Слово «advertising» стоит в тексте прямо.

items.quote: This is where a crowd of opinions becomes a single choice.
items.prompt: Paragraph D

explanation.en: The first sentence of paragraph D is its heading: many opinions become one choice → vii. The quorum is the mechanism, not the topic.
explanation.kk: D абзацының бірінші сөйлемі — оның тақырыбы: көп пікір → бір таңдау → vii. Кворум — тәсіл, тақырып емес.
explanation.ru: Первое предложение абзаца D и есть его заголовок: много мнений → один выбор → vii. Кворум — это способ, а не тема.

items.quote: Piping tells the cluster to warm its flight muscles, and about ten minutes later ten thousand bees lift off together
items.prompt: Paragraph E

explanation.en: Paragraph E runs from the quorum to take-off: the signal, warming the muscles, lift-off → i. Heading ii about the queen is wrong: the scouts set the direction.
explanation.kk: E абзацы кворумнан ұшуға апарады: сигнал, бұлшық етті жылыту, көтерілу → i. ii тақырыбы аналық туралы қате: бағытты барлаушылар көрсетеді.
explanation.ru: Абзац E ведёт от кворума к взлёту: сигнал, прогрев мышц, подъём → i. Заголовок ii про королеву неверен: направление задают разведчицы.

items.quote: Researchers have measured this by offering swarms a choice of wooden boxes of known size and following the colonies afterwards
items.prompt: Paragraph F

explanation.en: Paragraph F answers the question “does it work”: the box experiment and winter survival → vi. A poor choice is mentioned, but as part of the test rather than as the topic.
explanation.kk: F абзацы «бұл жүйе жұмыс істей ме?» дегенге жауап береді: жәшіктермен тәжірибе және қыстан аман шығу → vi. Нашар таңдау да айтылады, бірақ тексерудің бөлігі ретінде.
explanation.ru: Абзац F отвечает на вопрос «работает ли это»: опыт с ящиками и выживание зимой → vi. Про плохой выбор там сказано, но как часть проверки, а не как тема.

items.quote: The reason this small piece of natural history is quoted so often outside biology is the shape of the procedure rather than the bees.
items.prompt: Paragraph G

explanation.en: Paragraph G is about what people could take from the procedure: independent assessment, advertising in proportion, a quorum → viii.
explanation.kk: G абзацы — рәсімнен адамдар нені ала алатыны туралы: тәуелсіз баға, күшіне қарай жарнама, кворум → viii.
explanation.ru: Абзац G — про то, что из процедуры могут взять люди: независимая оценка, реклама по силе, кворум → viii.

headings.text: Turning a choice into a take-off
Why the swarm cannot stay where it is
Evidence that the choice is a good one
Keeping the cluster warm in winter

groups.instruction: Text 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs B–G from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i–ix.

items.quote: The cavity should hold about forty litres
items.prompt: What does a scout require of a cavity?

options.text: A wide entrance that is easy to find.
A volume of roughly forty litres.
A position close to water.
A site at ground level.

explanation.en: “The cavity should hold about forty litres” → B. The entrance should in fact be small and the site several metres above the ground, so A and D contradict the text.
explanation.kk: «The cavity should hold about forty litres» → B. Кіреберіс, керісінше, кішкентай болуы керек, биіктігі — жерден бірнеше метр, сондықтан A мен D мәтінге қайшы.
explanation.ru: «The cavity should hold about forty litres» → B. Вход, наоборот, должен быть маленьким, а высота — несколько метров над землёй, поэтому A и D прямо противоречат тексту.

items.quote: She is advertising it with an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be
items.prompt: What does the length of a scout’s dance show?

options.text: How far away the site is.
How long she spent inspecting it.
How highly she rates the site.
How many bees have already seen it.

explanation.en: “an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be” → C. Distance is also encoded in the dance, but by the straight run rather than by the length, so A is the distractor.
explanation.kk: «an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be» → C. Қашықтық та биде беріледі, бірақ ұзақтығымен емес, тік жүрісімен, сондықтан A — жаңылыстыратын нұсқа.
explanation.ru: «an effort proportional to how good she judges it to be» → C. Расстояние тоже закодировано в танце, но не длительностью, а прямым пробегом, поэтому A — подставной вариант.

items.quote: once about fifteen scouts are found at one site at the same time, that site has won
items.prompt: How is the final decision reached?

options.text: Every scout eventually dances for the same site.
The oldest scouts overrule the others.
Enough scouts gather at one site at the same time.
The queen visits the chosen site herself.

explanation.en: “once about fifteen scouts are found at one site at the same time, that site has won” → C. Option A is exactly what the text denies: “the bees do not wait for agreement”, and some scouts are still dancing for another site.
explanation.kk: «once about fifteen scouts are found at one site at the same time, that site has won» → C. A нұсқасын мәтін тікелей теріске шығарады: «the bees do not wait for agreement», кейбір барлаушылар әлі басқа жер үшін билеп жүр.
explanation.ru: «once about fifteen scouts are found at one site at the same time, that site has won» → C. Вариант A — именно то, что текст отрицает: «the bees do not wait for agreement», часть разведчиц ещё танцует за другое место.

groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

items.quote: A scout that is satisfied returns to the cluster and dances on its surface.
items.prompt: returns to the cluster and begins to 23 ____ on its surface

explanation.en: “returns to the cluster and dances on its surface” → dance. After “begins to” the base form is needed, though dances is also accepted: the word is what is checked, not the grammar of the gap.
explanation.kk: «returns to the cluster and dances on its surface» → dance. «Begins to» сөзінен кейін негізгі форма қажет, бірақ dances нұсқасы да есептеледі: сөз тексеріледі, қою грамматикасы емес.
explanation.ru: «returns to the cluster and dances on its surface» → dance. После «begins to» нужна начальная форма, но и dances засчитывается — проверяется слово, а не грамматика подстановки.

items.quote: The choice is settled by a quorum
items.prompt: settled not by agreement but by a 24 ____

explanation.en: “The choice is settled by a quorum” → quorum. The word “fifteen” sits nearby and looks like the answer, but the summary already names fifteen scouts separately.
explanation.kk: «The choice is settled by a quorum» → quorum. Қасындағы «fifteen» жауапқа ұқсайды, бірақ түйінде он бес барлаушы бөлек аталған.
explanation.ru: «The choice is settled by a quorum» → quorum. Слово «fifteen» стоит рядом и выглядит как ответ, но резюме уже называет пятнадцать разведчиц отдельно.

items.quote: producing a thin, rising sound that researchers call piping
items.prompt: making a sound called 25 ____

explanation.en: “a thin, rising sound that researchers call piping” → piping. The word has to be copied from the text exactly: spelling is what is being checked.
explanation.kk: «a thin, rising sound that researchers call piping» → piping. Сөзді мәтіннен дәл көшіру керек: мұнда емле тексеріледі.
explanation.ru: «a thin, rising sound that researchers call piping» → piping. Слово нужно переписать из текста в точности: емле здесь и проверяется.

items.quote: Piping tells the cluster to warm its flight muscles
items.prompt: warm their flight 26 ____

explanation.en: “warm its flight muscles” → muscles. The text has the plural, and that is what should be copied.
explanation.kk: «warm its flight muscles» → muscles. Мәтінде көпше түр тұр, соны көшіреміз.
explanation.ru: «warm its flight muscles» → muscles. В тексте множественное число, его и переносим.

groups.title: Choosing a new home
groups.summary: A scout that is satisfied with a cavity returns to the cluster and begins to 23 ____ on its surface, and the longer she keeps this up, the better she rates the site. Advertisements fade unless they are renewed, so weak sites lose their supporters. The decision is settled not by agreement but by a 24 ____: about fifteen scouts at one site is enough. The scouts then move through the cluster making a sound called 25 ____, which tells the other bees to warm their flight 26 ____ so that the swarm can leave.
groups.instruction: Complete the summary below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from Text 2 for each answer.

items.quote: most conversations held in English today take place with no first-language speaker present at all
items.prompt: Most conversations in English today involve no first-language speaker.

explanation.en: The statement repeats the text almost word for word → YES. The “three to one” ratio refers to the number of speakers rather than conversations, but that does not change the answer.
explanation.kk: Тұжырым мәтінді дерлік сөзбе-сөз қайталайды → YES. «Үшке бір» қатынасы сөйлеушілердің санына қатысты, әңгімелердің санына емес, бірақ жауапқа әсер етпейді.
explanation.ru: Утверждение почти дословно повторяет текст → YES. Соотношение «три к одному» относится к числу говорящих, а не к числу разговоров, но на ответ это не влияет.

items.quote: The dispute looks like a question about pronunciation, she writes, but it is really a question about authority
items.prompt: The disagreement between the researchers is mainly about pronunciation.

explanation.en: The writer presents this view as correct and supports it in the conclusion → NO. The trap is that the dispute really does look like one about pronunciation, as the text itself says.
explanation.kk: Автор бұл ойды дұрыс деп келтіреді және қорытындыда қолдайды → NO. Тұзақ — талқы шынымен айтылым туралы сияқты көрінеді, мәтін мұны әдейі ескертеді.
explanation.ru: Автор приводит эту мысль как верную и в выводе соглашается с ней → NO. Ловушка в том, что спор действительно выглядит как спор о произношении — текст прямо это оговаривает.

items.quote: But the published descriptions of what has to be taught have narrowed
items.prompt: Most teachers have now been trained to teach an international core.

explanation.en: The text talks about syllabuses and examinations, but says nothing about how teachers themselves have been trained → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Мәтін бағдарламалар мен емтихандар туралы айтады, ал мұғалімдердің дайындығы туралы ештеңе жоқ → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Текст говорит о программах и об экзаменах, но о подготовке самих преподавателей не сказано ничего → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: These are varieties with their own settled norms, their own literatures and their own generations of speakers
items.prompt: Some varieties of English outside Britain and the United States have norms of their own.

explanation.en: “varieties with their own settled norms” → YES. The writer presents this without objection, as part of his own picture.
explanation.kk: «varieties with their own settled norms» → YES. Автор мұны қарсылықсыз, өз көзқарасының бөлігі ретінде келтіреді.
explanation.ru: «varieties with their own settled norms» → YES. Автор приводит это без возражений, как часть своей картины.

items.quote: The examinations that decide admissions are slow to change and still reward a familiar sound
items.prompt: Examinations have kept up with the way English is now used.

explanation.en: “slow to change and still reward a familiar sound” directly contradicts the statement → NO. This is not NOT GIVEN: the writer states his position.
explanation.kk: «slow to change and still reward a familiar sound» — тұжырымға тікелей қайшы → NO. Бұл NOT GIVEN емес: автордың ұстанымы айтылған.
explanation.ru: «slow to change and still reward a familiar sound» — прямое противоречие утверждению → NO. Здесь не NOT GIVEN: позиция автора высказана.

items.quote: Examiners, universities and employers still listen with an ear trained on those models
items.prompt: Learners taught an international core find work more easily.

explanation.en: Employers are mentioned, but nothing is said about who finds work faster → NOT GIVEN. The text is about the standard people are judged by, not about the outcome of a job search.
explanation.kk: Жұмыс берушілер аталады, бірақ кім тезірек жұмыс табатыны туралы ештеңе жоқ → NOT GIVEN. Мәтін қандай стандартпен бағалайтынын айтады, жұмыс табу нәтижесін емес.
explanation.ru: Работодатели упомянуты, но о том, кто быстрее находит работу, не сказано ни слова → NOT GIVEN. Текст говорит о том, по какому стандарту судят, а не о результате поиска работы.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Text 3? Write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer, NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.

items.quote: Ask learners what they want, he says, and a large majority name a national model
items.prompt: Learners themselves ask to be taught a national model.
keywords: a large majority name a national model

explanation.en: “Ask learners what they want … a large majority name a national model” is Keel → B. Duarte says the opposite: a national model should not be the target.
explanation.kk: «Ask learners what they want … a large majority name a national model» — бұл Keel → B. Duarte дәл керісінше айтады: ұлттық үлгі мақсат болмауы керек.
explanation.ru: «Ask learners what they want … a large majority name a national model» — это Keel → B. Duarte говорит ровно обратное: национальная модель не должна быть целью.

items.quote: it is really a question about authority: who writes the textbooks, who sets the tests
items.prompt: The real issue is who has the authority to decide what is correct.

explanation.en: “a question about authority: who writes the textbooks, who sets the tests” is Oyelaran → C.
explanation.kk: «a question about authority: who writes the textbooks, who sets the tests» — Oyelaran → C.
explanation.ru: «a question about authority: who writes the textbooks, who sets the tests» — Oyelaran → C.

items.quote: Consonants at the beginning of words, and the difference between long and short vowels, cause real breakdowns when they go wrong
items.prompt: Tests show that some sounds interrupt understanding far more than others.
keywords: altered one feature at a time

explanation.en: The experiments that alter one feature at a time are Vrba → D. Duarte also names a set of important features, but hers comes from recordings of meetings rather than an experiment; the statement says “tests”.
explanation.kk: Бір белгіні өзгертіп жасалған тәжірибелер — Vrba → D. Duarte да маңызды белгілер туралы айтады, бірақ оныкі кездесу жазбаларынан шыққан қорытынды, тәжірибе емес; тұжырымда «tests» сөзі тұр.
explanation.ru: Опыты с изменением одного признака — это Vrba → D. Duarte тоже говорит о наборе важных признаков, но у неё это вывод из записей встреч, а не эксперимент; в утверждении стоит слово «tests».

items.quote: A national model should not be the target of teaching
items.prompt: Teaching should not aim at the speech of one country.
keywords: should not be the target of teaching

explanation.en: “A national model should not be the target of teaching” is Duarte → A.
explanation.kk: «A national model should not be the target of teaching» — Duarte → A.
explanation.ru: «A national model should not be the target of teaching» — Duarte → A.

options.text: Ana Duarte
Martin Keel
Ruth Oyelaran
Tomas Vrba

groups.instruction: Look at the following statements and the list of people below. Match each statement with the correct person, A–D.

items.quote: This simple arithmetic has an awkward consequence for language teaching, which has spent a century treating the speech of a minority as the target
items.prompt: Why does the writer give figures in the first paragraph?

options.text: To show that English is still spreading.
To question an assumption that teaching is built on.
To explain why learners choose English.
To compare two ways of counting speakers.

explanation.en: The figures are given for the conclusion that teaching aims at the speech of a minority → B. The spread of English is not discussed, so A misses.
explanation.kk: Сандар қорытынды үшін келтірілген: оқыту азшылықтың сөйлеуіне бағытталған → B. Ағылшынның таралуы талқыланбайды, сондықтан A жарамайды.
explanation.ru: Цифры приведены ради вывода: преподавание целится в речь меньшинства → B. Рост английского в тексте не обсуждается, поэтому A мимо.

items.quote: teaching to an international core leaves learners short of what they are actually measured against
items.prompt: What is Keel’s main objection to teaching an international core?

options.text: It is harder to teach than a national model.
It has no support in research.
Learners are still judged by a different standard.
It ignores varieties such as Indian English.

explanation.en: “leaves learners short of what they are actually measured against” → C. Keel says nothing about difficulty of teaching or about research.
explanation.kk: «leaves learners short of what they are actually measured against» → C. Оқытудың қиындығы мен зерттеулер туралы Keel ештеңе айтпайды.
explanation.ru: «leaves learners short of what they are actually measured against» → C. Про сложность преподавания и про исследования Keel ничего не говорит.

items.quote: English in Nigeria and India is not a stage on the way to something else.
items.prompt: According to Oyelaran, English in Nigeria and India is

options.text: a step towards a British or American model.
a variety with norms of its own.
too varied to be described.
changing faster than other varieties.

keywords: not a stage on the way

explanation.en: “not a stage on the way to something else” plus “their own settled norms” → B. Option A is exactly what she rejects.
explanation.kk: «not a stage on the way to something else» және «their own settled norms» → B. A нұсқасы — дәл ол теріске шығаратын ой.
explanation.ru: «not a stage on the way to something else» плюс «their own settled norms» → B. Вариант A — ровно то, что она отвергает.

items.quote: do not need the same pronunciation course, and pretending otherwise serves neither of them
items.prompt: What does the writer conclude in the final paragraph?

options.text: The argument has been settled by recent evidence.
Examinations should be abolished.
All learners need the same pronunciation course.
What a learner needs depends on where the language will be used.

keywords: stop treating the question as general

explanation.en: Two learners with different goals do not need the same course → D. Option A contradicts the first sentence of the paragraph: the question is not settled.
explanation.kk: Мақсаты бөлек екі оқушыға бір курс керек емес → D. A нұсқасы абзацтың бірінші сөйлеміне қайшы: мәселе шешілген жоқ.
explanation.ru: Два ученика с разными целями не нуждаются в одном курсе → D. Вариант A противоречит первой фразе абзаца: вопрос не решён.
